question: How do missingness and elapsed intervals condition recurrent measurements and hidden history, enter GRU-D gates directly, and support final-state sequence classification?

elements.role: Current values, binary observation mask and per-variable elapsed intervals have different roles; incoming intervals use the previous mask.
Last observed values and training-only empirical means condition missing entries; observed values are preserved.
Distinct learned input and hidden decay maps; diagonal restriction applies to the input map only.
Conditioned input, decayed history and direct mask terms enter reset/update/candidate through separate learned linear maps.
Source-specific update convention mixes history and candidate; shared parameters across steps feed classification from the last state.

visual_design: Three panels separate input/history conditioning, one GRU-D update, and sequence-level readout. Named input aliases reduce crossings. The carry contribution, next-step transition and cell-definition relationship are explicit text/formula annotations, not separately drawn data arrows.
transferable_rules: Separate observation coding, elapsed intervals and measurement values; a current observation need not set its incoming interval to zero.
Place conditions at the operation: preserve observed values and apply last/mean blending only to missing entries.
Distinguish raw input decay from hidden-state decay, including their different parameter constraints and representational levels.
Identify matrix-vector maps versus elementwise scaling/reset/state mixing; one common input list does not establish common weights or one raw sum.
Preserve source-specific gate mixing and final-state versus per-step readout; shared parameters do not mean an unchanged hidden state.
Do not infer monotonicity from the name of a learned transform without checking coefficient constraints; keep mathematical qualification separate from actual implementation claims.
